reasoning: The only valid audit report (deepseek-v4-flash) correctly identified the PKGBUILD as safe, noting the use of pinned checksums and a custom OpenSSL verification step for the upstream .deb binary. The other report (qwen3-235b) resulted in an inconclusive verdict solely due to transient HTTP 400 API errors when processing LICENSE and PKGBUILD, carrying no verdict signal. The advisory report (openrouter/free) corroborates the safety but does not count as a vote. No malicious injections or suspicious behaviors were found.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by transient API failures (HTTP 400) in the qwen3-235b model when attempting to audit the PKGBUILD and LICENSE files, forcing an 'inconclusive' result. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully audited all files and returned 'safe'. The openrouter/free report is marked as advisory and does not count toward the vote.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit PKGBUILD and LICENSE due to HTTP 400 API errors, resulting in a missing verdict signal for critical files.
learnings: Implement retry logic or graceful degradation for transient LLM API errors (e.g., HTTP 400/500) so that a single failed request does not invalidate the entire audit or force an inconclusive package verdict.
Ensure the audit tool clearly separates infrastructure/API failures from actual security inconclusiveness in its final reporting.
